level.title: Scaling & Security
level.description: How do you handle millions of users without crashing? Meet the traffic cops of the internet.

quiz_data.question: What is Vertical Scaling?
options: Adding more servers to a group
Upgrading a single server with more CPU and RAM
Stacking servers on top of each other

quiz_data.question: What is Horizontal Scaling?
options: Adding more identical servers to share the load
Laying servers flat on the floor

options: Because if one server crashes, the others can still handle the traffic

lessons.title: Horizontal vs. Vertical Scaling
lessons.content_md:
# Horizontal vs. Vertical Scaling ⚖️

If your website becomes incredibly popular overnight, your single server won't be able to handle all the traffic. It will crash under the pressure. You need to **Scale** (grow) your app.

There are two ways to do this:

## 1. Vertical Scaling (Scaling UP) 🏢
Imagine you have a small delivery van. Vertical scaling is like taking that van to a mechanic, stripping out the engine, and replacing it with a massive, turbo-charged monster engine. 

In the Cloud, this means keeping your **one server**, but upgrading it to have more CPU and RAM. 
- **The Problem:** A server can only get so big before you hit the physical limits of hardware. Plus, you have to turn the server off to upgrade it!

## 2. Horizontal Scaling (Scaling OUT) 🚗🚗🚗
Imagine you have a small delivery van. Instead of making it bigger, you just buy **10 more identical vans**. 

In the Cloud, this means keeping your small servers, but adding **hundreds of identical copies** of them side-by-side.
- **The Benefit:** There is no limit! If you need more power, you just add another server. This is the true power of the Cloud.

<flipcard front="🏢 What is the difference between Vertical and Horizontal scaling?" back="Vertical (Scaling UP) is making a single server bigger and stronger. Horizontal (Scaling OUT) is adding many more identical servers to share the load."></flipcard>

lessons.title: The Load Balancer: The Traffic Cop
lessons.content_md:
# The Load Balancer: The Traffic Cop 👮‍♂️

So, you chose **Horizontal Scaling**. You now have 5 identical web servers running your app.

When a user types your website address into their browser, which of the 5 servers do they connect to?

If all the users accidentally connect to Server #1, it will crash, while the other 4 servers sit around doing nothing!

## Enter the Load Balancer

To fix this, we put a **Load Balancer** in front of the servers. 

Think of a Load Balancer as a traffic cop standing at a massive intersection during rush hour.
- Car 1 arrives: The cop points them to Server A.
- Car 2 arrives: The cop points them to Server B.
- Car 3 arrives: The cop points them to Server C.

The Load Balancer ensures that the traffic is perfectly distributed so that no single server ever gets overwhelmed.

<flipcard front="👮‍♂️ What is the job of a Load Balancer?" back="A Load Balancer acts like a traffic cop, distributing incoming internet traffic evenly across multiple servers so no single server gets overloaded and crashes."></flipcard>
